support: Every week of rain through that roof works further into the bottom of the stack, and I doubt October will come soon enough for the two Gates.

WV12-P01.5.note: The author dwells on the dripping roof, the splitting wood and the late vote and doubts the boards will survive, which is concern for their fate rather than criticism, praise, amusement or mere longing.

WV12-P02.5.note: The narrator laughs at the swarm on the clothesline and still grins at the memory, and the bees keep turning up in comic places, so the feeling is amusement; since the hives are still kept, there is no loss to be wistful about.

WV12-P03.5.note: Read literally, her reply urges getting Rook covered before the fireworks because a bang could undo his training, which is worry, and she had planned the blanket ahead of time; nothing in it reads as irritation at Theo, thanks, amusement or longing.

support: On every windy night since the storm I have lain awake listening for the sound of falling brick from the hill, and each morning I look out to see whether the chimney is still standing.
